cards.text: Jesus has just come down the mountain with His twelve new apostles, and a huge crowd is pushing in just to touch Him (Luke 6:13-19). He looks up at His disciples and says, “Blessed are you who are poor,” and friend, I cost a QUARTER. So I am LEANING in.

cards.question: Jesus calls the poor blessed. What reason does He give them?

answers.text: Yours is the kingdom of God

cards.text: Next: “Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled.” Hungry NOW, filled LATER, like every baker who ever stood in front of my oven staring at the timer.

cards.question: Jesus flips it the same way for the ones who are crying: “Blessed are you who weep now, for you will ___.”

cards.text: Then the hard part: people hate you, shut you out, insult you and reject your name as evil, because of the Son of Man. That's not getting left out of the group chat, friend. That's getting left out AND talked about in it.

cards.question: When people treat them like that, what does Jesus tell them to do in that day?
True or false: Jesus says the reward for being hated because of the Son of Man will come here on earth.

cards.text: And Jesus says they're in good company, because their fathers treated the prophets in the same way. Getting hated for God's sake? That's a club with some VERY famous members.
Then Jesus flips the whole sermon like a cookie on a spatula: “But woe to you who are rich,” and friend, I'm standing on a GOLD base. I'm sweating.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the rich have already received their comfort.

cards.text: “Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger.” Same flip as the blessings, just running the other direction.

cards.question: Jesus has a woe for the ones who laugh now too. What does He say will happen to them?

cards.text: One more woe, and it's about something most of us would LOVE to have. Back in the drawer, I'd have traded my whole mustache for one nice review.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says woe to you when all men speak well of you.
The hated ones got treated like the prophets. For the ones everybody praises, Jesus says their fathers treated the ___ prophets in the same way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “But to those of you who will listen, I say:” and He's about to talk about enemies. Friend, when somebody opens like THAT, you put the cookie down and lean in.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the listeners to do about their enemies?

cards.text: Then He adds: do good to those who hate you. To the ones who HATE you? Friend, I've been a cookie stamper my whole life, and I have never been pressed this hard.

cards.question: Jesus keeps the same pattern going: ___ those who curse you.

cards.text: And pray for those who mistreat you. Then Jesus gets personal: someone strikes you on one cheek.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says if someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also.

cards.text: If someone takes your cloak, don't hold back your tunic, and give to everyone who asks you. So if somebody takes my apron, I offer up the HAT, and friend, that hat is half my height.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says if anyone takes what is yours, demand it back.

cards.text: Then Jesus sums it all up in one line, and it's one you've probably heard your whole life.

cards.question: What's the one line Jesus uses to sum up how to treat people?

answers.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you
Treat others the way that they treat you
Do good to others when they have earned it

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you?” Friend, I loved the people who loved me back for YEARS and thought I deserved a medal.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says even sinners love those who love them.

cards.text: Same goes for doing good to people who do good to you, and lending where you expect to be repaid, because even sinners do that. Lending to somebody who'll pay you back in full isn't generosity, friend, it's just a bank wearing an apron.

cards.question: So Jesus says to love your enemies, do good to them and lend to them, expecting ___ in return.
Jesus says then their reward will be great, and they'll be sons of the Most High. What does He say the Most High is like?

answers.text: He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked
He rewards the ones who have earned it
He blesses the ones who bless Him

cards.text: “Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.” Then quick ones: do not judge, and you will not be judged, and do not condemn, and you will not be condemned.

cards.question: Same pattern one more time: “Forgive, and you will be ___.”

cards.text: Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, poured into your lap. Friend, that's how I pack a cookie box, and the lid has NEVER closed.

cards.question: Jesus gives one last reason to give so freely. What is it?

answers.text: The measure you use will be measured back to you
Whatever you hold on to will be taken away
Your giving will be seen and praised by others

cards.text: And that's where we'll set the timer for now. Jesus isn't done teaching yet, friend, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "Blessed are you who weep now, for you will ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 17 quotes "Forgive, and you will be ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke 'I cost a QUARTER' depends on his 25-cent price sticker. Bakers are only known to know about the junk drawer from onboarding, and the price sticker isn't set up anywhere in this lesson, so the line doesn't say what it refers to. Being cheap to buy is also a different thing from being poor, so the comparison doesn't share the core action.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: Luke 6:22 opens with 'Blessed are you when people hate you…', but the card calls it 'the hard part' and never says Jesus calls these people blessed. The baker misses that this is a blessing. That also makes card 6's answer ('Rejoice and leap for joy') a lucky guess instead of a reasoned one.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'The Son of Man' appears for the first time with no simple word on who He is. Here it is Jesus speaking of Himself.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says 'When people treat them like that,' which points back to the earlier story card, and that card is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'They're in good company, because their fathers treated the prophets in the same way' makes 'their' read as the disciples' own fathers. In Luke 6:23, 'their fathers' are the fathers of the people doing the hating.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Getting hated for God's sake' renames the text's reason. Luke 6:22 says 'because of the Son of Man.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The setup ('something most of us would LOVE to have… one nice review') all but states the answer to card 14 (woe when all men speak well of you), so card 14 tests nothing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Jesus sums it all up in one line' (and card 10's 'the one line Jesus uses to sum up how to treat people') claims Luke 6:31 is a summary of the verses before it. The text doesn't say how 6:31 connects to them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
